weakest_line: And if you're here to stand for God's word, welcome to the Valiant.
one_fix: Cut the pile of quotes after Pascal and the channel plug. End on the Kierkegaard idea (God hides enough to leave love free) and one sharp question.

weakest_line: Because it was the only thing standing between a family and death.
one_fix: Actually answer the why. Show from the text that the lamb died in the firstborn's place and the blood was a sign (Exodus 12:13), then link it to 'Christ our passover' (1 Cor 5:7). Cut the Exodus backstory recap to do it.

weakest_line: So the next time someone asks you where Cain's wife came from, you'll know what to say.
one_fix: Replace the closing line with a real response prompt, for example taking on the obvious follow-up objection (why close-relative marriage was not harmful then), so the ending lands instead of just wrapping up.
Open on the text's puzzle instead of a sermon to the viewer, e.g. 'Why did God ask Adam where he was if He already knew?', and cut the lines that assume what the viewer has done.

weakest_line: People ask this in our comments all the time.
one_fix: Commit to one clear answer built around Cornelius instead of a three-part survey that ends in 'Christians still disagree'. Cut the signposting and the Sodom detour.
Cut the colleague-lies-about-you analogy and use that time to build the Peter vs Judas contrast that sets up the closing question.

weakest_line: Because it came from God, for God's purpose, and the text never presents it as a reward or a sign of approval.
one_fix: Cut the closing recap, which repeats a point already made twice. Pick one takeaway (power is not approval) and end on a sharper question tied to it, not the generic failures-or-prayer choice.

weakest_line: Some Christians also wonder about this question sometimes.
one_fix: Answer the 'forever' half of the hook head-on with text, and drop the loosely connected verse list (the thief, Revelation 3:20) that dodges it.

weakest_line: Every prayer you have ever prayed is an attempt to reach across a distance that was never meant to be there.
one_fix: Anchor the speculation in more of the text, such as the tree of life and Genesis 3:22, so each 'what would change' is shown from Scripture and not imagined.

weakest_line: So God gave us free will, and He tells us plainly which way to choose.
one_fix: Ground the answer in Genesis itself (what the tree was, the one command, what God said) and cut the hypothetical steal/covet argument, which is asserted rather than shown.
